documents.source_category: Interim Financial Statements for the Quarter ended 30th June 2026

financials_interim.notes: First financial_statements entry ever for this symbol -- single set of statements, no Group/Company split (standalone hospital, no subsidiaries indicated). p.2 income statement, p.3 balance sheet, p.5 cash flow (this is Q1 of the fiscal year, so the 'Period Ended 30 June' cash flow column is genuinely quarter-isolated, not cumulative). No line item is separately labelled 'Operating Profit' -- operating_profit is derived as Gross Profit + Other Income - Administration Expenses - Other Operating Expenses (396,509,569 + 1,373,624 - 253,255,763 - 65,448,755 = 79,178,675), which reconciles to the disclosed Profit Before Tax once Finance Cost is deducted. No finance income line is disclosed (interest income appears only as a cash-flow adjustment, not recognised separately in the income statement) -- entered as 0 rather than left blank since its absence from the P&L is confirmed, not an extraction gap. capex = Acquisition of PPE (30,427,945) + Capital WIP (631,423) + Capital WIP-Intangible (205,711) + Intangible Assets (276,000) = 31,541,079; excludes 'Acquisition of Right of Use Assets' (2,226,000), a lease-related cash outflow rather than conventional capex. total_liabilities = total assets (1,858,352,065) minus total equity (1,204,063,828). Source PDF is a scanned/OCR document with some garbled raw text; figures above are taken from the cleaner re-extracted tables and cross-checked against each statement's own totals (e.g. PBT reconciles from the derived operating profit).

interim_updates.note_text: Singhe Hospitals posted Rs.553.0mn revenue for Q1 FY2026/27 (quarter ended 30 June 2026), up 18.5% YoY, with gross profit growing even faster (+24.4%) as gross margin improved from 68.3% to 71.7%. However, that margin gain was entirely absorbed by overheads: administration expenses rose 28.9% (Rs.196.5mn to Rs.253.3mn) and other operating expenses rose 45.3% (Rs.45.0mn to Rs.65.4mn), leaving operating profit essentially flat (+0.2%, Rs.78.99mn to Rs.79.18mn) and PAT up only 1.7% (Rs.55.1mn to Rs.56.0mn) despite the strong top-line and gross-margin performance. EPS was unchanged at Rs.0.13.
interim_updates.gaps_note: This is the first interim entry for SINH -- no prior quarter has been entered, so no QoQ comparison is possible. YoY figures use the comparative column disclosed directly within this filing (p.2-3), not a separately stored Q1 FY2025/26 row. No 'Operating Profit' line is separately labelled in the income statement -- it is derived here from Gross Profit, Other Income, and the two expense lines (see financial_statements notes for the reconciliation). No finance income line is disclosed. The source PDF is a scanned/OCR document with garbled raw text in places; figures were cross-checked against each statement's internal totals before entry.
interim_updates.takeaway: A gross-margin improvement story that didn't reach the bottom line -- revenue and gross profit both grew strongly, but faster-growing administrative and other operating expenses absorbed all of the gain, leaving PAT nearly flat YoY. This filing contains no chairperson's commentary or MD&A, so the specific driver of the overhead growth (staffing, new facility costs, one-off items) cannot be confirmed from the document itself.
operational_highlights: Revenue Rs.553.0mn, up 18.5% YoY; gross profit Rs.396.5mn, up 24.4% YoY, with gross margin improving from 68.3% to 71.7%
Administration expenses rose 28.9% YoY (Rs.196.5mn to Rs.253.3mn) and other operating expenses rose 45.3% (Rs.45.0mn to Rs.65.4mn), fully absorbing the gross-margin gain
Operating profit essentially flat YoY (+0.2%); PAT Rs.56.0mn, up only 1.7% YoY; EPS unchanged at Rs.0.13
This is the first quarter entered into the database for this symbol -- no prior financial_statements or interim_updates rows existed before this one
key_drivers: The entire YoY story is a margin/overhead one: gross margin expanded 3.4 percentage points (68.3% to 71.7%) on strong revenue growth, but administration expenses (+28.9%) and other operating expenses (+45.3%) grew far faster than revenue (+18.5%), erasing the gross-margin gain by the operating-profit line

No chairperson's message or MD&A accompanies this filing (only the primary statements and brief notes), so the specific cause of the overhead growth cannot be confirmed from the document -- it could reflect new hires, facility expansion, or one-off costs

Right-of-use assets grew sharply (Rs.67.3mn to Rs.112.8mn since 30 June 2025) alongside a near-doubling of lease liabilities (current + non-current), suggesting new leased facilities or equipment that could plausibly explain part of the overhead increase, though the filing does not state this directly

_gaps: ebitda: depreciation_amortization not disclosed; EBITDA understated (= operating profit only)
